paragraphs.source_en: 3. The successive Pastoral phase presents a significant difference in economic strategies and is founded mainly on cattle and sheep herding. The early Pastoral sites dated to 7,500 BP are situated in the internal parts of the mountains whereas later Pastoral phases, before 5,000 BP, are characterised by semi-residential sites limited to the lake shores in the lowlands (Cremaschi & Di Lernia 1996b). With the increasing aridity after 5,000 BP the plains remain uninhabited and the settlement pattern was concentrated more on the seasonal use of mountain shelters and the development of the sites near the oases. Regarding the Pastoral material culture, there was an increase in the presence of undecorated pottery and a large use of grinding stones.

paragraphs.source_en: The lithic industry indicates a significant change in mobility based on longrange movements with the increasing use of non-local raw materials (Cremaschi & Di Lernia 1996b).

paragraphs.source_en: Although the climatic conditions were humid as early as the 16th-15th millennium BP, the period before 10,000 BP has not yet provided dated archaeological material testifying to human presence in the Central Sahara. The apparent lack of human presence before 10,000 BP could be due to the fact that excavated shelters were too wet, as shown by travertine formations which resulted from the abundant presence of water in the shelters. A large amount of lithic tools all over the Sahara suggest that the human presence before 10,000 BP cannot be excluded, but the industry outside the shelters, which was possibly related to this occupation, cannot be dated.
